title: Locus iste
description: Anton Bruckner's motet for the dedication of a church, "This place was made by God", in Latin, for 4 singers in his own four voice parts from the earliest known printing (1886). Calm and mostly soft: in the middle the basses rest while the other voices pass the words between them in chromatic chords, and a bar of silence comes before the quiet ending.

credits.words: the Latin gradual for the dedication of a church
credits.arrangement: Bruckner's own four voice parts (Vier Graduale, Vienna: Rättig, 1886)

licence.words: public domain: the gradual of the Mass for the dedication of a church ("Locus iste a Deo factus est, inaestimabile sacramentum, irreprehensibilis est"), an anonymous Latin liturgical text, sung as the 1886 first edition prints it under the notes, "æ" and its commas included
licence.tune: public domain: Anton Bruckner died 11 October 1896
licence.arrangement: Bruckner's own four voice parts as the first edition prints them (Bruckner died 1896; no editor is named; public domain): all 48 bars, every pitch, rhythm and rest as printed, in its printed key (C), the tenor written at its sounding pitch (printed in the treble clef an octave above). Ours: tied and same-pitch slurred notes sung as one (the soprano's F sharp in bars 41 and 42, the alto's B flat and C in bars 40 to 42, the tenor's A in bars 41 and 42, and the "fac-" of bars 46 and 47 in the soprano, tenor and bass); the dynamics and the tempo word (Allegro moderato) left to the singer, the tempo 60 to a crotchet (no metronome mark is printed); and breaths written in for beginners, each taking half a beat from the note before a new line: the soprano, alto and tenor before "sa-" in bars 15 and 19 (from the slurred end of "le"); the soprano and alto before "pre-" in bar 27, and with the tenor before "est" in bar 29; the bass, which has no printed rest in bars 1 to 4 and 5 to 20, before "a" in bars 2, 6, 31 and 35, at the printed comma "est, a" in bars 8 and 37, before the second "De-o" in bars 10 and 39, before "fac-tus" in bar 11, before "in-" in bars 12 and 16, and before "sa-" and "men-" of each "sa-cra-men-tum" (bars 14, 15, 18 and 19, the note re-struck on the new syllable); and everyone at bar 41, inside the twelve-beat melisma on "De-", singing the vowel again as "(e)-" (the alto's tied B flat re-struck), before "fac-" in bar 46 and before "est." in bar 48. For 4 singers only, as Bruckner wrote it: the tenor sings bar 21 alone, the basses rest for nine bars, and the chords need all four voices. Accepted exceptions (singable.py), all Bruckner's own writing: rule 4, the soprano's G5 on the "o" of "a De-o" (bars 7 and 36), F5 on "fac-tus" and "a De-" (bars 8, 9, 37 and 38) and F sharp 5 on "cra-men-" (bars 19 and 20), over the beginner soprano's E5, her C4 and B3 on "tus est" (bars 11 and 12), and the bass's B3 and C4 on "le sa-cra-men-" (bars 17 to 19), over the beginner bass's B flat 3, with their seconds near the edges of the ranges (the soprano's E5 and F5 in bars 7 to 9, 15, 19 and 36 to 38, her D4 in bars 11, 13 and 46 and 47, the tenor's E4 in bars 18 to 20); rule 5, the melismas Bruckner slurs (the alto's "le" in bars 14 and 18, "est" in bar 29, "De-" in bars 40 to 42 and "fac-" in bars 46 and 47; the tenor's "lis" in bar 28 and "De-" in bar 41; the bass's "De-" in bars 7 and 36, "le" in bars 13 and 17, "men-" in bars 15 and 19 and "De-" in bars 40 to 42), the bass's octave drops on "men-" (bars 15 and 19) and its octave and tritone in the "De-" of bar 40, its two leaps in the lines of bars 5 to 6, 34 to 35 and 40, the tenor's minor sixths up to "æ-" in bars 13 and 17 (D3 to B flat 3, E3 to C4) going on up a step, and its major sixth down from "tum" to "in-" across the rest of bars 16 and 17; and the alto's step on down after its fourth down to "De-" in bars 10 and 39; rule C at bar 20, B in the soprano or alto and the bass, the root of B major there, not C's leading note
